The rule restricts data-name-1 to a BASED entry, and BASED is confined to WS/LS/linkage at level 1 or 77 in both (2002 13.14.2 SR15 = 2023 13.16.3 SR16; 8.6.4 = 8.6.5 word-identical), so no CD record, no file-section or debugging-line reach. No 2002-only form or operand.

cases.reason: Format 7 identical (ADDRESS OF data-name-1 | identifier-5 ... TO identifier-6). 'Based data item' rests on 8.6.4 (2002) = 8.6.5 (2023), word-identical, and based entries are confined to WS/LS/linkage in both (2002 13.14.2 SR15, 2023 13.16.3 SR16); the TYPE route cannot carry BASED into a CD (see ALLOCATE SR1). 2023's inserted Format 8 (function-pointer) renumbers formats but does not alter Format 7.

cases.reason: COLLATING SEQUENCE phrase identical in both SORT formats. The ALPHABET clause's national branch in 2002 already has LOCALE [locale-name-2], NATIVE, UCS-4, UTF-8, UTF-16, code-name-2 and literal-phrase, the same alternatives as 2023, so 'an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence' ranges over the same set. The rule is about the alphabet, not about data-name-2, so the CD-table reach of Format 2 (SR15, reader's DIFFERENT) does not attach to it.

citations.quote: Alphabet-name-2 shall reference an alphabet that defines a national collating sequence

cases.reason: SORT Format 1 USING identical. The rule leans on the RECORD clause's fixed/variable determination: the three RECORD formats are the same (2023 adds only the BYTES synonym), the implicit-RECORD GR5 is word-identical, and record size GR3 differs only in naming 'variable-length data item' (2002) vs 'occurs-depending table' (2023); in 2002 the only variable-length data items a file record can hold are occurs-depending tables (no dynamic-length items in 2002), so the record sizes compared are the same. File-names only.

citations.quote: the file description entry for file-name-2 shall describe neither records smaller than the smallest record
the file description entry for file-name-2 shall describe neither records smaller than the smallest record
plus the sum of the maximum number of bytes in any variable-length data item subordinate to the record
plus the sum of the maximum number of bytes in any occurs-depending table subordinate to the record
